answer: Copying the same citations across 239 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 239 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the haven index resolves every citation against the ledge checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the relic audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 9 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
